findings.claim: Observed twice, not reproducible on demand: a --pin-tab session on the default local-launch path silently recovered onto a fresh blank tab instead of failing with tab_gone when its bound tab was closed externally, and the binding file was overwritten with the blank tab's targetId and pinned:true. Whether this is a live defect or an artefact of my test setup is UNRESOLVED.
findings.evidence: Driven against real Chrome with the debug binary from c4fc782. Sessions gate1589 and gateX: `--pin-tab navigate example.com`, bound tab closed externally via CDP /json/close -> `snapshot` returned "(empty page)" exit 0, `tab list` showed a new t2 about:blank, and ~/.agent-browser/<session>.target was rewritten to {targetId:<blank tab>, pinned:true}. COUNTER-EVIDENCE, gathered after: six later sessions (r1, r2, r3, s1, gateV, gateW) under the same command sequence, including one where the extra blank tab was closed first so the bound tab was the sole tracked page (ctate's stated precondition), all returned the correct tab_gone error with the binding preserved. My first root-cause hypothesis (launch paths never reach mgr.set_pin_tab, so BrowserManager.pin_tab stays false) is contradicted by those runs, where the pin is demonstrably enforced on a local launch. The patch experiment that appeared to confirm it (adding apply_tab_binding_on_attach_or_rollback at actions.rs:3535) is invalidated by the same variance and proves nothing. What is real: two captured instances of silent recovery plus a rewritten binding file. What is missing: the discriminating condition.
findings.layer: end-to-end path, CLI flag to manager enforcement on the local-launch entry point

findings.claim: Candidate: ctate's round-3 findings 1 and 2 might still be reachable at head.
findings.evidence: Finding 2 (sole pinned tab closes -> blank tab): forced the exact precondition on session s1 by closing the extra blank tab first, then closing the bound tab externally. Result: tab_gone error, empty tab list, binding file intact. Also correct on r1-r3 and over --cdp. Finding 1 (rollback): forced with a corrupted binding file; first and second commands both return the corrupt-binding error rather than acting on a neighbouring tab, and deleting the file rebinds the original target. Both refuted at the end-to-end layer.

findings.claim: ctate's round-3 finding 3 (Page.enable on a Memory-Saver-discarded tab during pin restore) is fixed in code by revive_and_enable_active, but the fix was not exercised.
findings.evidence: Chrome's Memory Saver discard could not be forced on demand in this environment, so the 30s-hang path was never driven. Static review (mine and codex's independently) agrees the call site now revives first via ensure_renderer_alive, matching tab switch and close. Named as a gap rather than assumed to work.
findings.layer: end-to-end path under a browser state I could not induce

findings.claim: No test can catch the finding above: all binding unit tests call mgr.set_pin_tab(true) by hand, bypassing the state-to-manager wiring, and both e2e tests (e2e_pin_tab_rebinds_after_daemon_restart, e2e_pin_tab_gone_error_and_recovery) attach over a ws_url via attach_pinned_session, exercising only the CDP path. The parity test asserts state.pin_tab, never mgr.pin_tab.
findings.evidence: grep of set_pin_tab production vs test callers (browser.rs:2992..3312 all hand-set); e2e_tests.rs:7731 and 7913 both use launch_binding_host + attach_pinned_session(&ws_url); parity_tests.rs:756-761 asserts state.pin_tab only.
findings.layer: test coverage of the flag-propagation path

findings.claim: Candidate: the new rollback could leave the session unusable or acting on the wrong tab after a binding-recovery failure.
findings.evidence: Forced the branch with a corrupted ~/.agent-browser/gateR.target. First command returns the corrupt-binding error; the second command returns the same error rather than silently acting on a neighbouring tab, proving the connection was torn down and the attach path re-runs. Deleting the file and re-running with --pin-tab rebinds the original target (1D3E0F17...). Refuted at the end-to-end layer, not by unit reasoning.

findings.claim: Two of the three round-3 fixes ship without any regression test: apply_tab_binding_on_attach_or_rollback and revive_and_enable_active on the restore path. Only the ensure_page guard has one.
findings.evidence: No test references or_rollback or revive_and_enable_active; the existing revive tests (test_tab_switch_revives_discarded_tab, test_tab_close_revives_discarded_successor, test_connect_all_discarded_revives_first_tab) cover switch/close/connect, not the pin restore path that regressed. The restore-path revive is exactly the seam an external reviewer already caught once.

findings.claim: close_current_browser clears launch_hash, iframe sessions, screencasting and mouse state, but not event_rx, fetch_handler_task, dialog_handler_task, pending_dialog or pending_pointer_release. Raised by the codex reviewer.
findings.evidence: actions.rs:1994-2014 vs field list at 367-412; reset_input_state (581) only resets mouse_state. Verified reachability empirically: after a forced rollback the next command re-enters the attach path, and subscribe_to_browser_events / start_fetch_handler / start_dialog_handler replace or abort the stale receiver and tasks on the next launch, so no wrong-tab or phantom-dialog behaviour was observable. Pre-existing: every relaunch path already goes through this function.

findings.claim: enable_domains_pub (browser.rs:753) has no callers after the fix replaced its only use with revive_and_enable_active. It is the exact unguarded primitive whose misuse caused round-3 finding 3, left exported for the next call site to reach for.
findings.evidence: grep -rn enable_domains_pub across cli/src returns only the definition. Independently enumerated by the codex reviewer (its lens 1: "No callers outside its definition").
findings.layer: API surface of a risky primitive

exemptions.claim: The rollback is not destructive for user-owned Chrome
exemptions.evidence: BrowserManager::close (browser.rs:1249) only sends Browser.close when browser_process.is_some(), so --cdp and --auto-connect sessions disconnect without shutting down the user's browser.
